page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.2 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. The primary hardware accelerator is a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance asymmetry. The instance excels in machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference speeds for both prompt processing and text generation using small 135M and medium 7B models. Conversely, general-purpose CPU performance is a notable tradeoff. Single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and compression tasks, consistently score in the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average range.

Given the high-density GPU acceleration paired with modest CPU performance, the g2-standard-8 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that offload processing to the GPU rather than relying on heavy CPU computation. It is highly suited for small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, and GPU-accelerated graphics rendering. It is less optimal for CPU-bound tasks such as software compilation, heavy text processing, or high-throughput cryptography.
